alt.en: A printed page of music and words, page 92, shown without its heading. Three lines of melody in 3/8, marked Brisk, Solo and Chorus, carry the words "O blow the man down, bullies, blow the man down! Way-ay, blow the man down. O blow the man down in Liverpool town! Give me some time to blow the man down." Five two-line verses follow, the first beginning "As I was a-walking down Paradise Street", then "There was another set of words to this shanty" and two more verses.
alt.es: Página impresa de música y letra, la página 92, sin su encabezado. Tres líneas de melodía en 3/8, marcadas Brisk, Solo y Chorus, llevan las palabras "O blow the man down, bullies, blow the man down! Way-ay, blow the man down. O blow the man down in Liverpool town! Give me some time to blow the man down." Siguen cinco estrofas de dos versos, la primera empieza "As I was a-walking down Paradise Street", y luego "There was another set of words to this shanty" y dos estrofas más.

caption.en: Blow the Man Down on page 92 of W. B. Whall's Ships, Sea Songs and Shanties (third edition, Glasgow, 1913): the version we sing, from the call "O blow the man down in Liverpool town!" to the sailor's run-in with a policeman in Paradise Street.
caption.es: Blow the Man Down en la página 92 de Ships, Sea Songs and Shanties, de W. B. Whall (tercera edición, Glasgow, 1913): la versión que cantamos, desde la llamada "O blow the man down in Liverpool town!" hasta el encontronazo del marinero con un policía en Paradise Street.

alt.en: A printed page, page 18 of "Music of the Waters". A paragraph begins "One of the best and jolliest quick-time songs, and certainly one of the most well-known, is "Blow the Man Down."" Below are six lines of melody in 6/8, marked Solo and Chorus, with the words "I'm a true English sailor, just come from Hong-Kong" and "Then we'll blow the man up, and we'll blow the man down", and a verse beginning "As I was a-walking down Winchester Street".
alt.es: Página impresa, la página 18 de "Music of the Waters". Un párrafo empieza "One of the best and jolliest quick-time songs, and certainly one of the most well-known, is "Blow the Man Down."" Debajo hay seis líneas de melodía en 6/8, marcadas Solo y Chorus, con las palabras "I'm a true English sailor, just come from Hong-Kong" y "Then we'll blow the man up, and we'll blow the man down", y una estrofa que empieza "As I was a-walking down Winchester Street".

caption.en: Blow the Man Down with its tune on page 18 of Laura Alexandrine Smith's The Music of the Waters (London, 1888), where she calls it one of the most well-known chanties, a song for hoisting the topsail-yards, and her sailor is "just come from Hong-Kong".
caption.es: Blow the Man Down con su melodía en la página 18 de The Music of the Waters, de Laura Alexandrine Smith (Londres, 1888), donde la llama una de las canciones marineras (shanties) más conocidas, una canción para izar las vergas de gavia, y cuyo marinero acaba de llegar de Hong Kong ("just come from Hong-Kong").

source: Laura Alexandrine Smith, The Music of the Waters (London: Kegan Paul, Trench & Co., 1888), p. 18
